evals.prompt: Tengo este archivo TypeScript de 814 lineas en monolithic/app.ts. Las sesiones de Claude Code son caras y lentas. Como reduzco tokens?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the monolithic file as the main problem, recommends splitting into files of max 150 lines, proposes a concrete split plan, and cites the 18.2% token savings from experiment data.
expectations: Identifies monolithic/app.ts (814 lines) as the primary source of token waste
Recommends a maximum of 150 lines per file as the target
Proposes a concrete split plan with specific file names and responsibilities
Cites the 18.2% token savings figure from experiment data
Mentions noise reduction (92% less noise on focused tasks)

evals.prompt: Mi CLAUDE.md tiene 800 lineas con docs API inline, snippets, y toda la arquitectura. Cada interaccion cuesta demasiados tokens.
evals.expected_output: Recommends keeping CLAUDE.md under 500 lines, explains lazy loading pattern, and mentions 50-70% reduction potential.
expectations: Recommends keeping CLAUDE.md under 500 lines
Explains the lazy loading pattern (triggers in CLAUDE.md, details in referenced files)
Mentions 50-70% reduction in token consumption
Suggests moving API docs and architecture details to separate referenced files
Recommends running /context to measure current token usage before and after

evals.prompt: Llevo 2 horas con Claude Code, esta lento, respuestas peores. Tengo 15 MCPs conectados. Que hago?
evals.expected_output: Recommends /clear or /compact for context reset, limiting MCPs to 10 or fewer, using subagents for verbose tasks, and strategic model selection.
expectations: Recommends /clear or /compact to manage accumulated context
Advises limiting active MCPs to 10 or fewer
Suggests using subagents (Task tool) for verbose operations
Mentions strategic model selection (Sonnet for routine, Haiku for simple tasks)
Explains that each unused MCP still costs tokens in tool descriptions

evals.prompt: Estoy llamando la API de Anthropic directamente desde mi backend en Node. Envio el mismo system prompt de 8K tokens en cada request y los costos se disparan. Como los reduzco?
evals.expected_output: Recommends enabling prompt caching with cache_control on the system prompt, explains pricing math (1.25x write, 0.1x reads), warns about cache-breaking pitfalls, and suggests verifying cache_creation_input_tokens.
expectations: Recommends enabling prompt caching via cache_control: {type: ephemeral} on the system prompt
Explains the pricing math (1.25x write cost, 0.1x read cost, pays for itself on second call)
Warns about cache-breaking patterns (images, timestamps/session IDs before breakpoint, toggling thinking)
Mentions the minimum token threshold per model (e.g. 2,048 for Sonnet 4.6) and verifying cache_creation_input_tokens in the response
Points to references/api-optimization-guide.md for full details

evals.prompt: Proceso 10,000 documentos por dia con Claude para clasificarlos. No necesito respuesta en tiempo real. Como reduzco el costo?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Batch API (50% off), routing simple classification to Haiku 4.5 instead of Sonnet/Opus, setting effort low or disabling thinking, and combining Batch with prompt caching for stacked savings.
expectations: Recommends the Batch API for 50% off on all token prices (since latency tolerance is >24h)
Suggests routing classification tasks to Haiku 4.5 instead of Sonnet or Opus
Recommends setting effort: low or disabling extended thinking for simple classification
Mentions combining Batch API with prompt caching for stacked savings (up to ~95%)
Suggests constraining output format explicitly (e.g. JSON with specific keys, no explanation) to reduce output tokens
